overview: OpenAI expands AI agents and collaborative tools, targeting workplace productivity.
New GPT‑6.1 Sol offers higher capability at lower cost for professional tasks.
AMD’s $8.2 B acquisition of World Labs strengthens its AI chip competition with Nvidia.

top.title: DevDay 2026 Recap
top.summary: OpenAI’s DevDay announced agents handling ongoing tasks, a shared ChatGPT surface for human‑agent collaboration, and native experiences for its 1.2 B weekly users.

top.title: Introducing GPT-6.1 Sol
top.summary: GPT‑6.1 Sol delivers near‑Astra performance on coding, document, and workflow tasks at roughly one‑fifth the cost, improving factual accuracy and efficiency.

top.title: Trump orders US government to call AI ‘Super Intelligence’
top.summary: President Trump signed an order renaming “artificial intelligence” to “Super Intelligence,” mandating federal use of the new term despite no regulatory changes.

top.title: AMD acquires World Labs AI startup, upping the ante against Nvidia
top.summary: AMD will acquire World Labs for $8.2 B, adding world‑model technology and research talent to compete with Nvidia in AI and robotics workloads.

top.title: OpenAI takes on Microsoft with the launch of what feels a whole lot like ChatGPT’s own office suite
top.summary: OpenAI unveiled “Space,” “Pages,” and “Slides,” AI‑enhanced collaborative office tools within ChatGPT, positioning itself against Microsoft’s productivity suite.

top.title: OpenAI launches Dots, its Muse competitor
top.summary: OpenAI introduced Dots, always‑on AI assistants powered by GPT‑6 Astra, capable of multi‑app tasks, learning preferences, and operating within ChatGPT Spaces.
